analysis: The only change in this PR is documentation: docs/provider/cli-reference.md gains one table row (hunk at head line ~1751) documenting DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP. It is described as an env var that the daemon forwards, where `0` disables load-time shape warmup and `always` skips its shader-cache probe. The supplied units (head lines 1-830) are unchanged surrounding text; the added row falls outside the visible excerpt, so I could not check it in context. No code, trust-boundary or authentication behavior changes. Relevant threats: T-041 (prefix-cache TTFT timing oracle, SEC-035). The new warmup variable affects latency and the shader cache, not cache scoping, TTL, HMAC lookup tags, salts or at-rest crypto. A load-time warmup runs synthetic inputs and does not touch consumer prompts (A-001). The documented env passthrough list does not include secrets. Open question for any code pass: the implementation in ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift (shapeWarmupEnvironmentKey) is not supplied here. Confirm that warmup never uses real consumer prompt data, never writes SSD prefix-cache artifacts with non-synthetic content, and that the shader-cache probe skip does not weaken any integrity check. This doc change gives no evidence of regression and introduces no new attack surface.
